explanation: This game's first pitch (commence_time) had already passed before the actual run that wrote the decisions listed in decisions_affected. The decision instants themselves (decision_utc) were honestly pre-game -- decision_time_for_game's own guard had nothing to object to -- but the RUN that wrote these rows did not happen until the observed write instant below, well after this game's first pitch. Prior to this fix, recorded_utc equalled decision_utc on every row (B1), so the ledger carried no evidence of when these rows were actually written; the write instant below is reconstructed from the commit that added these rows (git show -s --format=%cI 41c74c7399e68a8657183876bbf5cc3c31e6c2de) and the file's own mtime at that commit, both consistent. src.engine.slate.run_slate now refuses (skips, does not write) any game already commenced at the actual write instant in LIVE mode -- these rows were written before that guard existed and would be refused if the same run happened today. This row does not alter, replace, or remove the original decision rows -- the ledger is append-only and its history is preserved exactly as written; this is additional evidence appended after the fact, not a correction of the original bytes.
note: Appended by the B1/B2 fix (session https://claude.ai/code/session_01BB6CEj23fhPMVV2gLhkqz4). Has no `decision_utc` key at top level and `kind` != the sentinel every decision-reading consumer checks for, so it is skipped by src.engine.settle_slate.load_decisions, src.engine.slate._load_existing_decision_keys, and src.cli's `eod` command -- exactly like a genesis row -- and cannot be mistaken for a DecisionRecord or double-counted.
